key_insight: Automatic thematic indexing of literary corpora can be reframed as multi-label machine learning, with fine-tuned LLMs outperforming smaller encoder models on Voltaire’s works.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that scalable AI can reduce the manual burden of scholarly indexing and enable structured access to large historical text collections.
method: Formulate page-level thematic indexing as a multi-label classification task.
Compare encoder-based classifiers with LoRA fine-tuned generative LLMs from ~3B to 120B parameters.
Test both in-corpus performance and cross-corpus generalisation on two Voltaire sub-corpora.
evidence_signal: On the Essai sur les mœurs et l’esprit des nations and Questions sur l’Encyclopédie, the best Mistral-family model in 4-bit quantisation reached F1 scores up to 0.67.
watch_item: Reported scores may underestimate useful performance because human indexing is subjective and model outputs can be semantically valid even when they differ from the print index.
paper_title: Automatic Thematic Indexing of Large Literary Corpora: A Machine Learning Approach to Voltaire's Complete Works
